name: Jayant Infratech Limited
summary: Railway EPC has genuine historical scale, but negative cumulative cash conversion, collateral intensity and unresolved stress-funding claims dominate. GQS 5.0 after CASH cap; BQS/IAS NS, G3 unresolved. Conditional standalone base return is negative at the October 19 reference quote; proposed acquisition/promoter funding are not assumed complete.
identity_note: ISIN/BSE code and current10,336,686 issued shares reconcile revised annual and official master; no proposed acquisition shares included. [S1, S7, S12]

quote.kind: Secondary observed close, not live executable quote

score_note: Exact v3.0 arithmetic. BQS 92% coverage/bound 4.50–5.22; GQS raw5.65 capped5.0 for persistentCASH 3; IAS 30% coverage/bound1.60–7.90. No missing-weight reallocation.

gates.reason: RPT correction, allocation and presentation concerns need disciplined follow-through. Audits and reviewed filings do not establish severe diversion, manipulation or minority abuse. Non-cooperation is not default.

Signed core statements and detailed notes support bounded history and a full opening-claim model. RPT/tax/benefit classification and several boilerplate/comparative errors limit selected conclusions; no blanket rejection of all historical factors.

Essential no-growth stress can develop a2.3206 crore gap without rescue, while tax-credit access and unchanged-collection countercases survive. Bank scope, legal credit matching and dated claim settlements are not sufficiently resolved to establish either Pass or conclusive Fail. Optional acquisition failure alone is not used to fail this gate.

Trading observations support a coarse L 3 at ₹5 lakh, but secondary turnover proxies, six unknown sessions, lot size and lack of BSE-specific current restriction/depth verification prevent an executable-order conclusion.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Jayant is a real railway-electrification contractor that expanded annual revenue from ₹35.18 crore in FY2021 to ₹111.70 crore in FY2026. The obstacle is not a lack of awarded work but the amount of cash and collateral needed to turn it into shareholder returns. FY2026 reported PAT was ₹8.44 crore, yet CFO was negative ₹13.44 crore; cumulative cash conversion is also negative over three and five years. Retention/EMD and restricted FDs together tie up nearly ₹49.91 crore. [S1–S6]

At the secondary-source October 19 close of ₹126.71, equity value is ₹130.98 crore. A deliberately conditional standalone base produces about -0.56% annualised over five years, even after working-capital improvement; a favourable operating case produces 13.80%, below the 15% hurdle. Neither is a group fair-value conclusion because the proposed related-party acquisition and its funding are unfinished. [S8–S12]

Classification: evidence-constrained, funding-sensitive project contractor; hold off on an investment conclusion. BQS and IAS are NS, not neutral midpoints. GQS is 5.0 after the persistent weak-cash-conversion cap. G3 is unresolved: conservative essential-operation stress fails, but tax-access and unchanged-collection countercases survive. This is not a finding of an actual default. The decisive next evidence is a facility/claim reconciliation and verified project-cash realisation, not another headline order.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
As of 20 October 2026; last market session 19 October. Identity: Jayant Infratech Limited, BSE SME 543544, ISIN INE0KR801019, listed July 2022. Reporting perimeter is standalone under Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards. The existing 30% AOP interest is an investment; the proposed remaining 70% business is not included as completed consolidated revenue. Current issued capital is 10,336,686 shares, not the annual weighted-average EPS denominator. [S1, S8, S12]

Historical revenue/profit confidence is Medium across six years and High for directly reconciled current face statements. Cash classification and funding resilience are lower-confidence where legal recoverability or facility scope is unresolved. Forecast uncertainty remains separate from those historical-input labels. The acquisition funding/perimeter and consequential tax/RPT claim access are genuinely material gaps; ordinary presentation errors do not make every factor NS.

G1 Conditional; G2 Conditional; G3 Unresolved; G4 Conditional. The report supports a historical GQS comparison with its cap, but no BQS/IAS point ranking or investment approval. The 15% nominal pretax five-year equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh liquidity reference are research assumptions, not personal investment suitability or an allocation instruction.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 7, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 3, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 5. IAS factors: Q NS, R NS, D 3, P NS, L 3. Every factor has a claim-linked evidence trail and contrary evidence; the same factor is reused without changing weights.

BQS known contribution 4.42 at 92% coverage gives a missing-data bound 4.50–5.22, not a point score or confidence interval. GQS raw calculation is 7 ×0.40 + 6 ×0.20 + 5 ×0.15 + 4 ×0.15 + 3 ×0.10 =5.65. Persistent CASH 3 caps the final to 5.0. IAS known contribution 0.90 at 30% coverage gives 1.60–7.90, with no ranking midpoint. G3 is not forced to Fail just to impose an IAS cap; IAS is already incomplete for material funding/perimeter uncertainty.

REV starts 8 from the selected five-year CAGR of 25.99% and receives the permitted single-point current-trajectory downgrade after both comparable half-years contracted. No factor 9–10 is assigned. Moving MOAT and EXEC by one point changes the BQS bound by 0.20 and 0.08 respectively; those judgment sensitivities exceed small apparent peer-score differences. A one-point CAP change moves raw GQS 0.15 but does not remove the persistent CASH cap. These research-policy scores are not validated predictors of return, fraud or default.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
Jayant designs and executes railway overhead electrification, including 25 kV traction-related work, and provides maintenance. Track, signalling, civil and related works offer adjacent execution opportunities. Customers pay for contract progress and certified work, not simply for inventory procurement. Qualified execution, coordination with Railways and site work are important, but they do not eliminate tender competition or project delays. [S1, S6]

The earnings engine is contract revenue less materials/subcontracting, personnel and other execution costs. The funding engine is different: materials/WIP, supplier advances, retention and bank-guarantee collateral precede full cash collection. CARE describes partial payment against eligible material supply and retention continuing through completion/defect-liability obligations. This explains why an apparently asset-light plant base can still be capital intensive. [S6]

FY2026 operating EBITDA, excluding all other income, is ₹11.20 crore on ₹111.70 crore sales, about 10.03%. Restricted-deposit interest and AOP profit are real reported income but are not a second operating segment whose sales may be capitalised as contractor growth. The proposed AOP acquisition is analysed separately rather than assumed to improve all ratios automatically.

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
A two-decade operating history, railway execution credentials and customer relationships create a useful qualification barrier. A sizeable awarded book suggests the company can win work. Neither fact proves pricing power: project concentration, tendering and capital tied up in certification constrain durable excess returns. Three- and five-year incremental capital-return proxies are below the assumed capital-cost range. [S1, S6]

Three economic comparators illustrate the distinction. KEC has broad integrated railway OHE, signalling, traction, track and civil capabilities plus manufacturing integration. H.G. Infra remains road-led but has diversified into rail/metro execution. E To E Transportation describes systems integration across signalling, telecom and electrification with a newer safety-product OEM subsidiary. Jayant is smaller and more concentrated; it cannot inherit their scale, proprietary-product economics or stock-market multiples by sector association. [S13–S15]

Evidence that would strengthen MOAT includes repeat wins at attractive cash returns, customer-level retention, measurable qualification scarcity and stable margins without increasing collateral per rupee of work. Evidence against the thesis would be backlog growth coupled with chronically higher funding needs and no pricing advantage. Current MOAT 5 reflects useful but contestable capabilities, not a generic average.

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Annual operating revenue in crore: FY2021 35.1806; FY2022 38.2976; FY2023 42.4839; FY2024 89.3006; FY2025 121.7197; FY2026 111.6984. Annual rupee additions were 3.1170, 4.1863, 46.8167, 32.4191 and minus 10.0213 respectively. Five-year CAGR uses 35.1806→111.6984 over five actual intervals: 25.99%. Three-year CAGR uses 42.4839→111.6984: 38.02%. A ten-year comparable audited series is ND, not zero. [S1–S4]

Use the five-year issuer series rather than cherry-pick the faster three-year window. FY2021 pandemic conditions are acknowledged, but no unsupported numerical correction or extra small-base penalty is imposed. Historical AOP profit is outside operating revenue; the proposed acquisition has not been retroactively mixed into the series. Price/volume and organic project-cohort splits are not disclosed well enough for a precise decomposition.

FY2026 revenue fell 8.23%. Comparable first-half revenue fell about 0.94% from 55.1417 to 54.6249; second-half fell about 14.28% from 66.5780 to 57.0735. The two halves, not an isolated quarter, justify the REV trajectory deduction. FY2026 PAT edged up only 0.42%. Management attributes March execution/collection disruption partly to Railway payment-system technical issues; a subsequent banked recovery was not verified. No seasonal half-year is annualised into a fictional latest TTM.

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The annual report and CARE indicate substantial work access, but orderbook numbers are not interchangeable: management describes 500+ crore around March 31, while CARE reports 385.55 crore at July 31. FY2026 inflows 188.79 crore in the annual and 221.80 crore in CARE are not reconciled by a project-level opening/addition/execution/cancellation bridge. CARE also reports roughly 55% in three projects and 50% in Chhattisgarh. Treat these as dated scope-limited disclosures, not a single precise executable backlog. [S1, S6]

Accessible demand includes upgrades, private sidings, maintenance, track and signalling. With broad-gauge electrification already near completion, historic electrification opportunity cannot simply be extrapolated forever. The proposed AOP business may broaden capability, but its FY2026 ₹22.58 crore sales cannot be added to Jayant without overlap, acquisition timing and funding analysis. [S6, S8]

Operating capital, including restricted collateral/retention, rises from ₹29.56 crore in FY2023 to ₹89.36 crore in FY2026. Core NOPAT rises from ₹3.36 crore to ₹8.24 crore. Incremental return is 8.16% over three years and 9.13% over five, below an assumed 12–16% nominal cost-of-capital range. This is a deployment-timing-sensitive proxy, not a mature project IRR, but it does not support superior reinvestment economics. Base growth is financeable only with a significant WIP/retention/collateral-efficiency improvement.

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Nilesh Jobanputra is managing director/CFO; the disclosed board includes executive/family involvement and independent directors. Family control and related-party commerce are not themselves abuse. The important questions are transaction terms, minority economics, complete disclosure and disciplined allocation. Current beneficial-owner/pledge details were not independently reconciled to October 20; no clean-pledge assertion is made. [S1, S16]

Dated promise/delivery review: FY2024/FY2025 delivered substantial sales growth; FY2026 sales fell despite management's large-orderbook narrative. The April/May 2026 non-cash acquisition/share issue was withdrawn July 27 after non-receipt of SEBI approval and the earlier BTA terminated. October 1 introduced a cash ₹12.5667 crore proposal for the remaining 70% AOP interest. CARE says promoter funding is indicated after approvals, not received or priced. October 14 corrected timing; final signed timing remains unverified. [S1, S7–S9, S17]

The September 17 revised annual corrects enterprise-related purchases from ₹59.67 lakh to ₹1,978.09 lakh. The company calls this a technical/typographical error limited to that amount. It changes the scale of RPT exposure, not by itself the audit opinion or a finding of misconduct. Remuneration rose from ₹0.4440 crore to ₹0.7260 crore while PAT was flat. Other disclosed rent, salary and commission dealings reinforce the need for arm's-length discipline, without establishing abuse.

The financial audit is unmodified and reports no default/fraud. Secretarial reporting notes a late cost-auditor appointment and CRA-2 not filed at report date. Contradictory cost-record/working-capital-limit wording and irrelevant business labels constrain disclosure confidence. They are reported as presentation/compliance limitations with the issuer's explanations, not allegations of fabricated accounts.

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY2026 revenue 111.6984, core EBITDA 11.1989, core EBIT 10.9818 and reported PAT 8.4409 crore. Other income 2.2227 includes FD interest 1.4814, AOP profit 0.5996 and car-disposal gain 0.1330. A simple 25% tax core PAT proxy is 6.8057 crore, not audited adjusted PAT. Keep the 0.2115 crore firm-tax expense in operating costs until its nature is clear. Reported EPS 8.13 uses an unresolved weighted denominator; PAT/current issued shares gives 8.166, which is a different metric. [S1, S5]

Cash audit: 11.8765 pre-WC cash minus 22.4313 WC absorption minus 2.8803 tax = negative 13.4351 CFO. Adding CFI -3.4106 and CFF 16.8664 takes free cash 0.0330→0.0536. Cash capex 0.7867 is investing, not the cause of negative CFO. Three-year CFO/PAT is -0.087x; five-year is -0.281x. Interest is financing cash flow, so cash after interest/capex is weaker. [S1–S5]

Opening assets 121.4681 and equity 59.7465 crore reconcile to all disclosed debt/claims. Gross debt 32.9807 includes term current 0.1142/noncurrent 0.4369, overdraft 32.4295 and 0.0001 rounding. Ordinary WC 38.4694 includes all payables, statutory/salary/expense balances, customer advances and refundable security deposits 14.6629. Runoff of those deposits consumes cash; they are not silently free financing. Current tax 2.7593 and current gratuity 0.0006 are separately paid; noncurrent gratuity 0.1227 is retained as a terminal claim. No future service cost cancels that legacy amount. [S1]

FD 22.5836 and retention/EMD 27.3296 are operating/collateral capital, not free cash. Tax-authority asset 4.9147 is excluded from central cash and terminal value, with a separate legal/timing-accessible tax-offset case applied once against old/new tax. DTA 0.0477 is not monetised. Related advances-taken 4.2745 lack a clean face mapping: central retains all face OCL, then tests reclassifying a subset into repayable interest-bearing finance and, separately, adding a conservative non-overlapping claim. These are analyst alternatives, not discovered omitted debt.

Receivables older than six months rise 0.6751→3.1892 crore. A prior-year ageing-table total, annual ratio denominators and PPE headings contain presentation inconsistencies; face/signed comparative statements govern the model. A 0.0151 crore tax contingency conflicts with no-disputed-dues wording and is stress-paid separately. Bank guarantees 10.9701 are contingent, not ordinary debt; a 10% call test is isolated to avoid double-counting contract losses. No unpaid tax or guarantee default is inferred.

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Observed reference ₹126.71 on 19 October 2026 gives market cap ₹130.9761 crore. Using March 31 debt 32.9807 and free cash 0.0536, dated EV is ₹163.9032 crore: 15.52times reported PAT, 19.24times core PAT proxy, 14.64times core EBITDA and2.19 xbook. These are not October cash/debt observations; net debt/core EBITDA is 2.94 times and core EBIT/interest 5.76 times. No peer multiple is imported automatically. [S1, S11, S12]

The linked monthly model rolls audited March 31 stocks through FY2027–FY2031 plus a stub ending 19 October 2031. April–October 2026 is forecast, not observed cash. It funds maintenance, WC, retention and FD collateral; pays all current taxes/benefits and debt interest; amortises the small term loan; assumes renewal but no increase of the existing revolver; retains legacy gratuity. Central interest 10%, FD yield 5.5%, cash tax 25%, maintenance capex 0.6% of sales, and no dividends. Future restricted FD interest is taxed but FD principal is not spendable.

Base: revenue growth 10%, 12%, 12%, 10%, 8%, then 8% forward; 10% EBITDA margin; WIP/sales 32% then 30%, 45-day receivables, supplier advances 7%, retention 23.5% and restricted FD 20% of sales. These are improvements, not neutral assumptions. At 8 xterminalcore EBIT, terminal price ₹123.22, minimum cash ₹0.4654 crore and five-year IRR -0.56%. If WIP/retention/collateral efficiency does not improve, growth creates a ₹15.20 crore shortfall and no IRR.

Bull: 18%, 18%, 16%, 14%, 12%, then 10% growth; 11% margin; 29% WIP, 35-day receivables, 21% retention and 18% FD collateral; 10 times EBIT. Terminal ₹241.86, minimum cash ₹1.4297 crore, IRR 13.80%. The bear execution-delay case is unfunded; it has no shareholder IRR. A flat, unchanged-efficiency countercase survives but returns -12.79% annualised at 6 times EBIT. Financed tax-access stress survives but returns -19.55%.

The base terminal bridge is EV 152.4407 + cash 6.2516 + investment book 1.2296 - debt 32.4295 - legacy gratuity 0.1227 = equity 127.3697 crore, divided by 1.0336686 crore shares. Restricted FD, retention, tax assets and DTA are not added again. Base entry diagnostics for 12%, 15%, 18% hurdles are ₹69.92, ₹61.27, ₹53.87; these are conditional calculations, not buy levels overcoming unresolved gates.

Every reverse test reruns funding. At 6, 8 and 10 times EBIT, no funded 15% return crossing exists on a 0–40% annual-growth grid at base margin/stock assumptions. Faster growth can worsen financing. Optional acquisition outflow without verified funding creates ₹10.08 crore gap; hypothetical equity at ₹100 or ₹80 grossed for 3% fees funds it but dilutes holders. No unverified target profit is used to sweeten those cases. Final R, P and IAS remain NS until investable-perimeter and claim-funding questions are resolved.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The central risk chain is project certification or collection delay → more WIP/receivables and locked guarantee collateral → dependence on revolver renewal or promoter capital → dilution/claim seniority and weaker equity recovery. The historical evidence supporting stress is negative cumulative conversion, a latest-year revenue decline, larger aged receivables and concentrated projects. This is a credible financing mechanism, not an allegation of present default. [S1, S6]

Separate avoidable expansion from survival. A restrained case stops growth, maintains the opening inventory/retention/collateral ratios, uses 0.45% sales maintenance, assumes existing revolver renewal, 50-day receivables rather than 37.5 and 8% EBITDA rather than 10.0. It develops a ₹2.3206 crore minimum-cash shortfall. At 8% interest the gap remains ₹2.0735 crore. Collection slippage alone produces ₹1.4720 crore gap; margin stress alone 0.4059. No arbitrary inventory write-down is stacked into this credible survival test.

Counterevidence matters: unchanged collections and margins survive with minimum cash ₹0.2476 crore; allowing the opening tax-authority asset to offset legally matching old/new tax once makes the stressed path survive at ₹0.2564 crore. Because that asset's nature/timing and current bank scope are not sufficiently disclosed, G3 is Unresolved rather than mechanically Pass or Fail. CARE's adequate-liquidity assessment is disclosed, not ignored; its reported accruals and historical utilisation are not extra drawable cash.

A separate severe boundary removes revolver renewal, cuts revenue 25%, reduces margin 6% and adds 10% opening inventory/receivable loss. Its ₹44.70 crore gap is a remote stress boundary, not the sole basis of the gate. The impairment is noncash once; replacement WC is funded once. A 10% bank guarantee-call test is separate because it may overlap underlying project losses. Optional acquisition funding failure alone cannot establish insolvency of existing essential operations.

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold price outcomes over five years require 38.0% and 58.5% annualised shareholder returns before any dilution. From current market cap ₹130.98 crore, target equity values are ₹654.88 crore and ₹1309.76 crore. Holding the base cash/debt bridge, 8 times exit EBIT and base forward operating margin fixed implies revenue around ₹882 crore and ₹1732 crore, respectively. These are arithmetic requirements, not forecasts.

Using five years from FY2026 revenue for a transparent scale illustration implies roughly 51.2% and 73.0% annual revenue growth. At an illustrative 75% incremental operating/collateral-capital intensity, incremental funding would be around ₹578 crore and ₹1215 crore before retained profits or financing. Actual timing differs from the exact five-year market-price horizon, which the full return model handles.

Such growth requires wins, execution capacity, certification, collateral and bankable collections simultaneously. The existing capital record and funded reverse tests do not establish this. Using a higher terminal multiple merely shifts the burden to sustained superior economics; unpriced promoter equity dilutes per-share upside. No credible financed 5×/10× case is demonstrated, and no probability is invented.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
At the next financial release, compare operating revenue and core margin with matched half-years rather than annualising a seasonally favourable period. Track cash receipts separately from order announcements. A useful improvement would be positive rolling CFO after interest, reduced WIP/retention days and no new tax/employee/deposit settlement gap; rising revenue with larger cumulative funding deficits would contradict the improvement thesis.

Before an investment decision, obtain the actual facility-wise sanctioned/drawn/available statement and maturity schedule, reconcile March overdraft with later rating scope, verify security FD encumbrance and release terms, and identify the legal nature/timing of ₹4.9147 crore revenue-authority assets. Reconcile ₹4.2745 crore RPT advances taken to face liabilities. Refresh borrower stress with dated payments and no assumed unreceived rescue.

For the acquisition, verify the corrected annexure, approvals, final BTA, consideration adjustment, target standalone balances/earnings, promoter funding type/price/receipt and actual closing. Evidence of cash receipt does not remove dilution or repayment terms. Separately confirm updated cost-filing status and resolved disclosure corrections. Refresh BSE lot/trading restrictions and real turnover/depth at the actual position size before implementation. These are analytical checkpoints, not automatic trades, contact requests or scheduled monitoring commitments.

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Evidence-constrained, funding-sensitive project contractor; not a demonstrated compounder or an established multibagger. Historical GQS 5.0 is ranking-eligible only as a capped growth-quality comparison with Medium confidence. BQS and IAS are not point-ranked because material BAL/per-share funding evidence is missing. G1/G2/G4 are Conditional and G3 is Unresolved.

Conditional action: do not convert a modest reported P/E or a large orderbook into an allocation. First establish whether essential operations remain funded under realistic settlement/collection timing and whether any acquisition capital is received on acceptable per-share terms. Then rerun the 15% hurdle at a current quote and the user's actual size. A lower price can improve expected return, but cannot by itself make inaccessible collateral spendable or resolve unpriced dilution.

The conditional standalone model already shows why waiting for evidence is substantive: base working-capital improvement still yields a negative return at the reference quote, while favourable operations yield less than the stated hurdle. Conversely, supported tax-credit access or proven collections could improve survival. Neither the favourable case nor the adverse case is presented as certain.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Source priority is the September 17 revised signed annual, issuer historical annuals and visually checked scanned results, then signed transaction filings and dated rating rationales. Secondary market histories are explicitly separated from exchange-verified security identity. The unrevised issuer annual is not used for the corrected RPT purchase amount. Official primary BSE copies that returned 403 were not bypassed; signed public filing mirrors supplied the key revised annual and transaction notices. [S1–S12]

Unresolved items: October 14 corrected acquisition timing; final approvals/funding/closing; actual available bank lines; tax-credit legal matching and settlement timing; RPT liability mapping; retention/FD release; latest beneficial ownership/pledges; orderbook/inflow scope bridge; comparative ageing/weighted EPS/provision presentation; current BSE surveillance/depth. These gaps have specific consequences: no final group valuation, selected factors NS and G3 unresolved, not indiscriminate suppression of audited history.

Analyst assumptions include 25% tax,10% central borrowing rate,5.5% collateral FD yield, maintenance/reinvestment ratios, monthly cash timing, future collection/retention ratios,6–10 xterminalEBIT, no central incremental facility and no completed acquisition. Opening/closing stocks and each tax/employee/interest/legacy claim are mapped once. All monthly cash/debt/WC/share identities, annual rollups, terminal claims and caps are checked. Model shortfalls and conservative exclusions are our analytical constructions, not new issuer accounting findings.

GOV.reason: Audited profitable operations and withdrawal rather than completion of the unapproved share-swap are positive. A major RPT correction, repeated presentation weaknesses and an unresolved related-party acquisition funding structure constrain demonstrated stewardship. No diversion or fraud is alleged.

MOAT.reason: Railway execution credentials, customer access and a sizable awarded book are useful qualifications. Tender competition, concentrated project geography and capital tied up in certification/retention limit evidence of durable excess economics; larger integrated and specialised competitors remain credible.

REV.reason: Choose five-year reported comparable issuer revenue before scoring:25.99% CAGR starts 8. Both comparable FY2026 half-years declined, supporting the permitted minus1trajectory adjustment. Three-year CAGR is disclosed, not substituted for a higher score; no automatic small-base penalty.

DUR.reason: Modernisation, private sidings, maintenance and track/signalling create multiple demand avenues and a substantial awarded book. Near-complete broad-gauge electrification shifts the mix toward upgrades; concentrated execution and collateral funding constrain access. Proposed AOP revenue is not guaranteed incremental runway.

CAP.reason: Three- and five-year incremental operating-capital returns around8–9% fall below the assumed 12–16% capital-cost range, with large WIP, retention and guarantee collateral. Profitable historical scaling and potentially releasable project capital are contrary evidence, but do not yet establish superior returns on fresh deployment.

CASH.reason: Negative cumulative CFO/PAT over both three and five profitable years, FY2026 inventory/advance absorption and increased aged receivables establish recurring weakness. Positive FY2024/FY2025 CFO and latest receivable release are acknowledged; they do not offset persistent cumulative shortfall. CASH≤3GQS cap applies.

BAL.reason: NS for a consequential funding question, not for a minor table error: restrained no-growth collection/margin stress has a cash gap, but plausible tax-credit accessibility reverses it and actual bank facility scope is unreconciled. Free cash is tiny; CARE adequate-liquidity evidence is contrary to an automatic Fail. Neither rescue funding nor unused limits is verified.

EXEC.reason: Multi-year delivered revenue scale and substantial orders demonstrate real execution capability. Latest revenue contraction, inconsistent orderbook/inflow scopes and a withdrawn/reworked acquisition show uneven delivery and disclosure discipline. Management attributes March delays to Railway payment-system issues; later cash collection is not independently proven.

EARN.reason: Core EBITDA improved substantially over five years and FY2026 PAT held up despite lower revenue. However non-operating FD/AOP income is material, current-share EPS is not reported weighted EPS, and recent operating profit barely grew. Warrant forfeiture is capital reserve, not profit growth.

R.reason: NS final investor-return factor: standalone conditional base IRR is negative, but acquisition economics/funding and accessible tax/RPT claims materially affect the investable perimeter. Conditional diagnostics remain visible rather than pretending they establish a financed group return.

D.reason: Audited assets and a flat operating countercase provide some recovery capacity, unlike an unsupported zero-value assumption. Low free cash, collateral lock-up and a credible collection stress with financing needs make downside resilience weak; the tax-access countercase still loses roughly 19.5% annualised. No current default is asserted.

P.reason: NS final price-expectations factor because final acquisition funding/per-share economics are not established. Standalone reverse tests are demanding and do not clear 15% at6–10xEBIT on a funded0–40% growth grid; proposed promoter money cannot simply be counted without dilution/claims.

L.reason: Observed-only theoretical exit17.75 days and conditional missing-zero sensitivity19.22 days both fall in the10–20 day band. Use its lower3: no orderly-depth evidence,750-share lot and seven one-price observations. The much stronger last20sessions do not replace the more conservative60-session reference.

Q.reason: BQS incomplete because BAL is NS; no missing weight is redistributed.

confidence.forecast_uncertainty: high uncertainty, separate from historical input confidence

valuation.status: Conditional standalone diagnostics; final IAS not scored
